title: Dualizing complex of the point
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions], with $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. On the bounded constructible point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] of the identity is naturally isomorphic to the identity. In particular,
$$
\omega_{s,\Lambda}=Ra_s^!\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_s.
$$
For every $C\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ put $c=\operatorname{Fib}_s(C)$, using the point fibre equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and define $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s(D_sC)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)=c^\vee.
$$
Here $c^\vee$ is the derived coefficient-module dual of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]. At finite and integral coefficients the evaluation on the left means termwise sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ on the ambient derived category, as in [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; at $E$ it means its rationalization, and at $\Qlb$ it means its common finite-stage version. Thus this formula spells out $D_sC\cong C^\vee$ under the point-category identifications, rather than identifying a sheaf complex with a coefficient-module complex without evaluation.

proof.text: Choose the compactification $s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s$. The formula $Rf_{!,n}=Rp_*j_!$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is the identity here, since direct image and extension by zero along the identity act termwise as the identity. At the integral stage the formula of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] is $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n C_n\cong C$ by derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete]. The natural unit into this total limit is the reduction/limit adjunction unit [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; its composites to all levels are the original reduction maps. The normalized reduction tower has the canonical counit isomorphisms of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Write these functors as $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$, with unit $u$ and counit $e$. Since $e_N$ is invertible for normalized $N$, the triangle equation $\mathcal L(e_N)u_{\mathcal L N}=1$ makes $u_{\mathcal L N}$ invertible. Derived completeness supplies some isomorphism $h:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L\mathcal R C$; naturality gives $u_{\mathcal L\mathcal R C}h=\mathcal L\mathcal R(h)u_C$, so $u_C$ is invertible as well. Thus the canonical natural unit, rather than a separately chosen completeness isomorphism, identifies integral identity compact support with the identity functor. The natural isomorphism $u^{-1}$ descends to the rational category: naturality for an integral arrow $v$ gives naturality for $v\otimes a$ after multiplying both sides by $a$, and hence for sums of such arrows. For descent to the common-stage category, check compatibility with $E\subset L$. The completed scalar comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies integral scalar extension with ordinary derived tensor by the finite free completed coefficient sheaf. Tensor by this sheaf commutes with the products and cones in the total-limit model: after a choice of basis it is a finite direct sum, so the identification acts componentwise. On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, the canonical completion map has the reduction maps as its product component and zero as its shifted-product component, exactly as specified in that comparison. Tensoring this map and applying the coefficient comparison yields the completion map for the extended representative, with the same reduction and zero components. Thus the square formed by scalar extension, the compact-support scalar comparison, and the two units $u$ commutes as an equality of chain maps, not merely after projecting to each reduction. Its inverse square gives the same compatibility for $u^{-1}$. At a common field the naturality square is therefore the rational naturality square already proved; extending that field preserves its equality. This gives a natural identity normalization of $Ra_{s!}$ in all four point categories. Use the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ of [def-pod-conventions, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], which that definition records as a theorem rather than a part of the definition; for $f=a_s$ it is supplied stage by stage as follows. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, take the compactification $c=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$ with $\dim s=0$ in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], clause 2: there $P_c=Ra_{s!,n}$ and $R_c=\nu_s^*a_s^{\times}R\nu_{s,*}=Ra^!_{s,n}$, and every $K\in D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$ has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii), so $\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{s!}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)$ naturally for $K,L\in D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$, the categories being full. At $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, the separated finite-type morphism $a_s$ of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] gives $G_{a_s}$, with the object formula $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRa^!_{s,n}L_n$ of the integral exceptional functor, right adjoint to integral $Ra_{s!}$ on $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$. At $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ the finite-Tor categories are by definition the bounded constructible ones, and [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients] gives the natural adjunction $Ra_{s!,\Lambda}\dashv Ra^!_{s,\Lambda}$ on them. For any $K,L$ in that category, its natural Hom bijection becomes $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$. Write the resulting natural bijection as $\Phi_K:\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$. Set $u=\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(1)$ and $v=\Phi_L^{-1}(1)$. Naturality in $K$ gives $uv=1$ and $\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(vu)=u=\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(1)$, hence $vu=1$ by injectivity. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism; naturality of the original bijections in $L$ makes it a natural isomorphism. At $L=\Lambda_s$ it gives $\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_s$. This concerns the constructible adjoint, not the comparison composite on arbitrary pro-etale complexes.

source.place: first sentence: identity compact support and uniqueness of its constructible right adjoint

proof.text: The coefficient DVR theorem [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] applies; its principal-ideal property makes $\mathcal O_E$ and its quotients Noetherian. For the finite and integral cases write $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$. Let $\underline M$ be the constant sheaf and set $L_R(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] makes the constant module functor exact; at finite level $L_R(M)=\underline M$, and at integral level flatness of $B$ over $\underline R$ [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] makes $L_R$ exact. Sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. The continuous-coefficient description [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] gives $\Gamma(s,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})=C(\{*\},\mathcal O_E)=\mathcal O_E$. The reduction theorem identifies $B/\varpi_E^n B$ with $(A_{E,n})_s$; multiplication by $\varpi_E^n$ is injective on $B$, since $\mathcal O_E$ is a domain and $B$ is flat. Exact sections therefore identify $\Gamma(s,(A_{E,n})_s)=A_{E,n}$, through the canonical constant-value map. Thus in both cases $\Gamma(s,B)=R$. There is an explicit adjunction $L_R\dashv\Gamma(s,-)$: a map $v:L_RM\to F$ gives $m\mapsto v_s(1\otimes m)$; a linear map $t:M\to F(s)$ gives $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U$ on every object $U$. Balancing and sheafification make the latter a sheaf map. The formulas are inverse and natural, and their termwise versions commute with the complex differentials.

These exact functors act termwise on derived categories. For a finitely presented $R$-module $M$, apply the two exact functors and sections to a presentation $R^a\to R^b\to M\to0$. Since $\Gamma(s,B)=R$, the adjunction unit identifies $M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,L_RM)$. Exactness then makes the unit an isomorphism for every complex whose cohomology modules are finitely presented. Noetherian finite modules are finitely presented [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]. At finite level, $L_R$ sends a complex with bounded finite cohomology to a complex with constant finite cohomology sheaves. Their geometric stalks are finite by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk], so this complex is constructible by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. At integral level every bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology over the DVR $R$ is perfect: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] gives $R^a\twoheadrightarrow M$ with finitely generated kernel; the kernel is torsion free as a submodule of a free module, so [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes it finite free. Thus each cohomology module has a length-one finite-free resolution, and [lem-sf-perfect-cohomology-assembly] gives a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ of the complex. The integral stratified-perfect characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], applied to the single stratum $s$, puts $L_RP=B\otimes_R P$ in $D^b_c(s,R)$. Here $s$ is Noetherian of dimension zero and $\ell\ne p$. Now take $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$ and $c=\Gamma(s,C)$. Its bounded finite/finite-generation properties are part of the target of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. We have proved $L_Rc$ is constructible. The adjunction triangle identity makes $\Gamma(s,L_Rc\to C)$ inverse to the unit at $c$, hence an isomorphism. Conservativity of the equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] therefore makes the actual adjunction counit $L_Rc\to C$ an isomorphism. This justifies replacing $C$ by $L_Rc$, without treating all pro-etale sheaves as coefficient modules.

source.place: second sentence, with its point-category identification made explicit

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution $B\to I$ for [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The complex $\Gamma(s,I)$ is K-injective over $R$: if $Q$ is acyclic, exactness of $L_R$ makes $L_RQ$ acyclic, and the termwise adjunction identifies a map $Q\to\Gamma(s,I)$ with a map $L_RQ\to I$, homotopic to zero by [def-pur-kinjective-complex]; the adjunction sends that homotopy back to a homotopy. Exact sections make $R=\Gamma(s,B)\to\Gamma(s,I)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $\Gamma(s,I)$ is a K-injective resolution of $R$.

source.place: K-injective Hom-complex construction preceding Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective; exact-left-adjoint argument written explicitly

proof.text: Represent $c$ by a coefficient-module complex and $C$ by $L_Rc$ using step 3. The derived internal Hom is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_B(L_Rc,I)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Its sections have terms $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_B(L_Rc^p,I^{p+j})=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_R(c^p,\Gamma(s,I^{p+j}))$ by the adjunction of step 2. Naturality makes the differentials on both sides $d_I\circ f-(-1)^j f\circ d_c$, as in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Therefore these are isomorphic as complexes, not merely as their cohomology groups. Step 4 identifies the right complex with a representative of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)$. Together with step 1 this gives $\Gamma(s,D_sC)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)=c^\vee$ [def-pod-perfect-point-complex], naturally in $C$, at finite and integral coefficients. No finite projective representative of $c$ was required in this computation at finite level. At integral level, use the bounded finite-projective model $P$ from step 3. Termwise sheaf Hom from $L_RP^i$ is a direct summand of a finite power of the identity functor, hence exact. The finite total Hom complex therefore sends an acyclic second input to an acyclic complex: filter by the finitely many degrees of $P$, whose successive quotients are shifted exact Hom complexes. Consequently $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_RP,B)\to\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_RP,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its source is $L_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R))$, a bounded finite-projective model, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] puts the internal Hom itself in $D^b_c(s,R)$. This verifies the domain required for its rationalization in step 6.

source.place: Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective, and the Hom-complex definition; adjunction identifies every term and differential

proof.text: At the rational stage represent $C_E$ by an integral object $C$ as prescribed by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Step 3 supplies a bounded finite-projective $R=\mathcal O_E$ complex $P$ representing $c=\Gamma(s,C)$. Rationalizing the isomorphism of step 5 gives $\Gamma(s,R\mathcal Hom_R(C,B))\otimes_R E\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R)\otimes_R E\cong\operatorname{Hom}_E^\bullet(P\otimes_R E,E)$; the last isomorphism is [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect]. This is the required $E$-coefficient formula, including inputs whose chosen integral representatives have torsion. An arrow $u\otimes a$ acts on the dual by precomposition with $u$ and multiplication by $a$ on both sides, so naturality holds on the localized morphisms. For algebraically closed coefficients represent $C$ by $(E,C_E)$ and compute the unit and internal Hom at that same finite field, as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The displayed isomorphism then defines the claimed arrow at stage $E$. To check independence of stage, choose a common finite extension $L$ for any input arrow. The fibre scalar comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identifies its coefficient complex with $c_E\otimes_E L$. To identify the internal-Hom comparison itself, use the completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] on the bounded finite-projective model $B\otimes_R P$ of step 3 and its dual model from step 5. Ordinary completed-ring extension then acts termwise on these models. Take the internal-Hom scalar comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] to be the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation. For a finite free term, evaluation on a basis gives $f\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto f(x)\otimes ab)$; passage to the image of a splitting idempotent gives the identical formula for a finite-projective term. There are finitely many terms, so these formulas identify the total Hom complexes and commute with their signed differentials. Sections of this map have the displayed module scalar-Hom formula, since the point-sections comparison is the inverse of the sections-tensor map followed by completion. Thus this calculation identifies the comparison used by the common-stage construction, beyond merely giving an abstract isomorphism of its source and target. Precomposition by a map of models commutes with this formula. For $E\subset L\subset M$, both successive scalar comparisons send $((f\otimes a)\otimes b)(x\otimes t)$ to $f(x)\otimes abt$. The internal-Hom comparisons and fibre comparisons have these same identity and composition compatibilities [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Hence the two stage representatives give the same arrow after extension to $M$, and an arrow represented over $L$ has the same naturality square there. This proves the common-stage formula with the specified, rather than arbitrary, coefficient comparisons.
